messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Serving runtime pool `us-west-2` — elevated pod restarts (85% of runtime pods restarted in last 5m). Symptoms: CUDA OOMs, container CrashLoopBackOff, node flaps. Autoscaler activity detected: multiple rapid scale ups/downs. Paging oncall: @oncall-ryan

oncall-ryan: I'm on it. Which customers are impacted? Any obvious error spike in the LB?

maya: looking at runtime logs now. see massive `cudaMalloc` failures followed by SIGABRT. snippet from one pod: ```
I tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:XXXX] failed to allocate 7.8 GiB (out of 8.0 GiB)
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
/var/log/runtime/runtime_main: FATAL: unhandled exception -> CrashLoopBackOff
```

raj: autoscaler logs show repeated scale events: +40 nodes -> -38 nodes within 6m. cluster-autoscaler eviction + pod reschedules likely causing KV cache thrash. suspect policy cooldown too low and spike-based scaling reacting to transient bursts.

elena: can we cordon the most flappy nodes to stop churn while we triage? we should also consider setting a temporary min-replicas to avoid scale-to-zero oscillation.

platform-sre: agree cordon + drain high-failure nodes. I'm running a quick query to identify nodes with >3 runtime restarts in 10m.

platform-sre: nodes identified: ip-10-0-45-12.usw2, ip-10-0-87-99.usw2, ip-10-0-64-21.usw2. cordoning now:```
sudo kubectl cordon ip-10-0-45-12.usw2
sudo kubectl drain ip-10-0-45-12.usw2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

oncall-ryan: doing short list of mitigations: 1) cordon/drain flappy nodes 2) bump autoscaler cooldown + set minReplicas=5 for runtime pool 3) route heavy customers to fallback smaller models 4) restart runtime process on remaining nodes gradually.

maya: prepared runtime restart script: ```#!/bin/bash
set -e
for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l app=runtime -o name | shuf); do
  kubectl exec $pod -- /usr/local/bin/restart-runtime.sh || true
  sleep 12
done
```
I can run a rolling restart with a 12s gap to reduce simultaneous KV cache rebuilds.

cs-aliya: customer impact: support telemetry shows ~12 customers with increased 95p latency and 2 customers experiencing 5xx errors for model inferencing. labeling two accounts as Tier-1 and contacting AMs. ETA for mitigation?

oncall-ryan: ETA 20-30m for initial containment (cordon + minReplicas + autoscaler tweak). maya please start the rolling restart. raj, can you propose autoscaler config change?

raj: suggest these temporary changes (applied to cluster-autoscaler HPA-like config):```
scaleDownDelayAfterAdd: 600s  # increase cooldown to 10m
maxNodeProvisionTime: 15m
minReplicas: 5
stabilizationWindow: 600s
```
This should stop the rapid oscillation. also recommend disabling aggressive scale-to-zero for runtime pool.

deploy-bot: SYSTEM: applying autoscaler patch to runtime pool `runtime-pool-usw2` by @raj. patch id: acp-311223-01.

deploy-bot: SYSTEM: autoscaler config applied.

platform-sre: autoscaler config change rolled in. monitoring for scale events.

maya: starting rolling restarts now. running script against 28 runtime pods. I'll watch for error regression in logs and CUDA OOMs.

maya: update: after ~7 pods restarted, observed a ~30% reduction in OOMs. still seeing occasional cudaMalloc failures on older nodes.

oncall-ryan: good. I'll also flip traffic routing to favor quantized v1.2-fallback model for noisy customers. that reduces GPU memory footprint.

deploy-bot: SYSTEM: traffic routing change executed: model-route `customer-heavy` -> `v1.2-fallback` by @oncall-ryan.

cs-aliya: notifying affected customers and AMs now. messaging template: "We're mitigating a serving disruption in us-west-2; we've routed you to a lower-memory model to preserve availability. We'll follow up with details and ETA for full recovery."

raj: note — we should not only bump cooldowns; followup: examine pod scheduling fragmentation. some pods are landing on smaller-instance GPU nodes with insufficient headroom. add a soft nodeSelector to prefer large-gpus temporarily.

elena: doing that now: adding nodeAffinity to runtime deployment: ```
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    - weight: 100
      preference:
        matchExpressions:
        - key: gpu.size
          operator: In
          values:
          - a100-40gb
```

platform-sre: applied affinity tweak. will monitor scheduler evictions.

incident-bot: UPDATE: incidents/incidents-3112234455 — mitigation in progress. cordoned 3 nodes, autoscaler cooldown increased, minReplicas=5, rolling restarts underway, traffic routed to fallback models.

maya: final quick log sample post-mitigation: ```
[INFO] 2026-03-15T21:13:12Z runtime: allocation succeeded for 3.2 GiB
[INFO] 2026-03-15T21:13:45Z runtime: inference latency p95 decreased from 2.9s -> 1.1s for routed customers
[WARN] occasional cudaMalloc(1024MB) failed on ip-10-0-64-21.usw2; node under investigation
```

oncall-ryan: are we ready to stop paging? still want to keep watch for 30m and keep minReplicas locked.

cs-aliya: still seeing improved latencies across 10/12 affected customers, two Tier-1s now stable. I'll keep the comms channel open.

platform-sre: monitoring shows no scale-down events in last 8m. cluster stability improving.

oncall-ryan: okay — stand down pages for now but keep incident open for postmortem. @all — please add any follow-ups to the incident checklist: root cause (cuda OOMs + autoscaler oscillation), short-term mitigations enacted, follow-ups (autoscaler tuning, node sizing, better model routing logic, throttling bursty tenants).

elena: I'll open a runbook PR for autoscaler damping + node affinity for runtime pools.

maya: I'll prepare logs and flamegraphs for the CUDA allocation failures and file an issue for runtime memory limits per-model.

raj: will run a simulation test to reproduce autoscaler oscillation with synthetic burst traffic and propose permanent config.

deploy-bot: SYSTEM: incident handoff scheduled to next oncall @oncall-jeremy at 3112234789.

oncall-ryan: handing off — summary: CUDA OOMs triggered crashloops; rapid autoscaler scaling made node fragmentation/warmup bad -> more OOMs. Containment: cordoned flappy nodes, increased cooldown & minReplicas, node affinity to larger GPUs, rolling runtime restarts, routed heavy customers to fallback quantized model. Customer impact: ~12 customers increased latency, 2 Tier-1 had 5xx — now stable. Follow-ups: autoscaler tuning, node sizing, model memory budgeting, improved routing throttles.

incident-bot: RESOLVE: incident flagged for postmortem. add label `postmortem-required` and move thread to `postmortems` channel once written. :white_check_mark:
